title: The quiet art of letting go
subtitle: A visual reflection on attention, release, and guarding the honor of others from backbiting.

sections.text:
Backbiting (ghibah) means speaking about a person in their absence in a manner that they dislike[cite: 18].

True or false, faults mentioned behind someone's back carry serious spiritual weight.

The Qur'an compares backbiting to eating the flesh of one's dead brother, emphasizing how indefensible the act is[cite: 19].

Every word is recorded, and careless speech can waste accumulated good deeds[cite: 20, 21].

People often backbite out of peer pressure, venting anger, envy, or even false sympathy[cite: 19].

Recognizing these underlying motives is the first step toward transforming your habits.

A believer's duty is not just to abstain from backbiting, but to defend the honor of an absent brother or sister[cite: 22].

Choosing silence or changing the subject safeguards both your character and your community.

Sincere repentance involves stopping immediately, feeling regret, and seeking forgiveness from those wronged[cite: 23].

Purify your tongue and carry that clarity into every conversation.
